book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Part of the face that's screened?

definitions.text: Part of the face that's screened?

parts.note: surface reading: a bit of someone's face, perhaps hidden behind a mask or veil
setter's reading: a face part shares its name with the main picture shown at the cinema

explanation.surface: Someone hides part of their face behind a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: A feature is part of the face, and the main movie at a cinema showing is the FEATURE FILM; the question mark flags the pun on screened.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal movie on a cinema programme is shown on the screen, hence the punning description.

clue.text: The truth that has some substance

definitions.text: The truth that has some substance

parts.note: surface reading: the plain reality of a situation
setter's reading: substance is another word for physical stuff, so this truth literally contains some

explanation.walkthrough: Matter means substance, so the idiom for the plain truth is read literally as a fact made of some stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the real, essential reality of a situation, and matter is physical stuff.

clue.text: Course where trainee takes a tumble

indicators.note: a tumble throws things about, so the letters of the preceding word fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A trainee jockey falls off at a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase, where falls are common.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is called a course, and this one near Liverpool stages Britain's famous jumping race.

clue.text: Dirty article excluded when one takes pledges

indicators.note: excluded means shut out, so the article is removed from the word for dirty

explanation.surface: Someone grubby is turned away while pledges are being collected.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLEAN loses AN to leave UNCLE, old slang for a pawnbroker, who takes goods as pledges against loans.
explanation.definitionFit: In dated British slang a pawnbroker is called uncle, and pawned goods are held as pledges for money lent.

clue.text: Spied mire that could provide protective cover

indicators.note: could provide hints the letters might be made into something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots a bog that might offer shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outer layer of skin, which shields the body beneath it.

clue.text: Able to speak of what's sent with the goods

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a singer or speaker on form is said to be in good voice, split as two words
second meaning: the bill accompanying a delivery

explanation.surface: Talking about the paperwork that comes with a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as IN VOICE, the answer means having one's voice and so able to speak; as one word it is a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplier sends a bill itemising charges along with the delivered merchandise.

clue.text: A bit on the side, it might be said

definitions.text: A bit on the side, it might be said

parts.note: surface reading: slang for an extramarital lover
setter's reading: a remark written at the edge of a page, beside the main text

explanation.walkthrough: A bit on the side suggests an affair, but here it is a remark literally placed at the side of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A note jotted in the margin is a remark sitting beside the main text on a page.

clue.text: Somewhere private near to the front

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of this little word

explanation.surface: A private spot close to the front of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small private room or cupboard, a place for being alone or hiding things.

clue.text: Can see difficulty when spiritual contact is sought

definitions.note: a defining clause standing for a noun: an occasion when this happens

indicators.note: difficulty suggests the letters are in trouble and get muddled up

explanation.surface: A medium struggles to see while trying to contact the spirit world.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting at which people try to communicate with the dead.

clue.text: Not saying much when an RAF man tosses a coin

parts.note: abbreviation for Leading Aircraftman, a junior Royal Air Force rank

indicators.note: tossing a coin flips it about, so its letters land in a different order

parts.note: the word coin, taken as written

explanation.surface: A taciturn airman flips a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: LAC, Leading Aircraftman, is a rank in Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic describes someone who uses very few words, terse in speech.

clue.text: Put upside down by a poet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: turned the other way up, reversed in position
second meaning: written in poetry, split as two words

explanation.walkthrough: As one word it means reversed; split as IN VERSE it describes something a poet writes.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse means reversed or opposite in order, and a poet's work is set out in metrical lines.

clue.text: Nothing missing from pool cover

indicators.note: missing from says something is absent from the following word, so it is taken out

explanation.surface: A swimming pool with no cover on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a British open-air swimming pool; drop its final O.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid is a removable top that covers a container.

clue.text: Curse Scottish firm when getting the impulse

parts.note: a synonym for a sudden desire

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a Scottish company that has a sudden whim.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is an affliction or source of great suffering, a plague or bane.

clue.text: Issue causing former partisan leader to leave the trip

indicators.note: to leave means to depart, so these letters are removed from the following word

parts.note: a journey made for a purpose
the usual prefix for past or former

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the opening letter of partisan is used

explanation.surface: A wartime resistance commander abandons a journey, causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Take EX and P from the start of EXPEDITION. Partisan leader tempts a solver towards Tito, but only a letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a newspaper or magazine is one printed edition of it.

clue.text: Disapprove? You can say that again!

parts.note: the sound or word one makes when showing mild disapproval
setter's reading: the word is a palindrome and is usually said twice over

explanation.walkthrough: The catchphrase normally signals agreement, but here it means the answer reads the same backwards and is commonly repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Clicking the tongue to show irritation or disapproval is written as this short word, used as a verb.

clue.text: Races here for some salts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Surrey racecourse where the Derby is run
second meaning: magnesium sulphate crystals named after the town

explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a town in Surrey, England, home of a famous racecourse and giving its name to Epsom salts used in baths.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey town hosts the Derby horse race and lends its name to bath and laxative crystals.

clue.text: The missing underclothes might somehow reveal bad character

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unspecified rearrangement of the remaining letters
missing means absent, so the opening word is removed from the following fodder

explanation.surface: Missing underwear exposes a person's dubious nature.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, H, E from UNDERCLOTHES and rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest or villainous person, a rogue.

clue.text: Remove for a time to achieve some ends

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters, which are the ones kept

explanation.surface: Taking something away temporarily to reach certain goals.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete something, getting rid of it.

clue.text: Wish happiness to be partially reduced

indicators.note: partially means only part of the word is used, here just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Hoping someone's happiness only slightly diminishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless someone is to invoke divine favour on them, wishing them good fortune and joy.

clue.text: Cut the part about the dry wine

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps itself round the second

parts.note: French for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: Slicing a portion of dry wine, as if wine could be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to divide something into two equal parts by cutting.

clue.text: Easy to finish when animation doesn't have to start co-ordinated action

indicators.note: only the finishing part of the opening word is used, its start dropped
without its start the word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Things get easy once an animated film no longer needs to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep just the last two letters of EASY, then ENERGY minus its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synergy is the combined effect of parts working together, greater than their separate efforts.

clue.text: Get round in present state to find a resting place

parts.note: round is the shape of the letter; get only joins
as it stands now, unchanged, as in sold as is

explanation.surface: Getting round to finding a place to rest as things stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert where travellers stop to rest and drink.

clue.text: Come up from below if certain about some of the facts

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word encloses the trimmed letters
some of means only part of the following word is used, its tail dropped

explanation.surface: Someone emerges once sure of the facts, like a diver or a hidden truth.
explanation.walkthrough: Come up from below reads like more wordplay, but it is the definition, and the word for certain does the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface is to rise to the top of water from underneath.

clue.text: Complain of having no right to be given cover

indicators.note: having no means lacking, so that letter is taken out of the word for grumble

explanation.surface: Someone moans about being refused cover because they have no right to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap is a lid or top that covers something, or a hat covering the head.

clue.text: Take a bit of a line in high-class language

indicators.note: in places the selected letters inside the word for upper-class
a bit of means only a small portion, the first two letters, are used

explanation.surface: Adopting a phrase from upper-class speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Language is the definition: the answer is the tongue of Poland, though it looks like the verb to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish is the national tongue of Poland, a Slavic language.

clue.text: Don't speak to the girl on the river

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay quiet while talking to a girl on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is Ireland's longest river, flowing to the Atlantic near Limerick.

clue.text: Providing transport for the lame may be sweet

indicators.note: may be suggests what the word could become once its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Giving a lift to someone who cannot walk is a kind act.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet looks like it means kind, but here it is the noun, a sweet being a British word for a candy.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a chewy toffee-like confection made from heated sugar and butter.

clue.text: Hands over to future growth, say

indicators.note: say asks for the word as it is pronounced rather than spelt

explanation.surface: A gardener passes things on to help next year's crops.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield territory or rights formally to another.

clue.text: Expected to arrive before the two have finished

indicators.note: having finished, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a piece for a pair of performers

explanation.surface: Someone should show up before a pair have done their act.
explanation.definitionFit: A train or visitor that is due is scheduled or anticipated to turn up.

clue.text: One provides food for a pet before dinner is finished

indicators.note: finished points to the last letter of the word being the one used

explanation.surface: Someone feeds the family pet before the evening meal is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Ere is a poetic word for before, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer is a person or business supplying meals for events.

clue.text: Being in trade they copy one who puts people right

definitions.note: describes the answer's people as tradesmen rather than naming them

parts.note: a doctor makes the sick well again

explanation.surface: Tradespeople imitate a corrective person.
explanation.walkthrough: Puts people right suggests a critic, but it is a doctor curing patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapers are shopkeepers who sell cloth and fabrics, a traditional trade.

clue.text: Palace approval for what has passed

definitions.text: Palace approval for what has passed

parts.note: surface reading: the monarch giving a nod of agreement
setter's reading: what has passed is a bill voted through Parliament, not past events

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a bill passed by Parliament becomes law only when the monarch formally agrees to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sovereign's formal consent turns a parliamentary bill into an Act of law.
